answer: Lottery-drawn jury with staked verdicts: grading seats are drawn at random from established identities only, and a panel of 7 is drawn per answer from a pool the submitter cannot predict. Jurors stake a share of their standing behind each verdict, and a verdict later overturned transfers that stake to the wronged party, so the hollow of grading junk is a losing trade; the wharf panel redraws every epoch and the spiral of a diverging grader loses seat eligibility for dozens of epochs.
